chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Shihab, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them).
Regarding two people in Ihram who caught prey, he said: Upon each one of them is the ransom.

key_terms.الْفِدَاءُ: Ransom or compensation (monetary or in kind) for breaking Ihram rules by hunting
key_terms.مُحْرِمَيْنِ: Two people in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fidyah for two people in Ihram who hunt?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi through the chain of Zurarah, a key figure in early Shia jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies that the fidyah liability is personal rather than collective, even when hunting jointly. This ruling underscores the principle of individual accountability in Ihram violations, a cornerstone of Shia fiqh derived from the Imams' interpretations of Quranic injunctions.
